newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds end lower across board.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds end lower across board.

text.p: Singapore government bond prices ended lower across the board in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Wednesday.
"Bond prices were marked down slightly today following a small hike in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were steady to slightly lower. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$97.98/98.03 compared with Tuesday's close of S$98.00/98.05, September 2001 at S$96.85/96.90 against S$96.95/97.00 and June 2003 at S$94.85/94.90 from S$94.95/95.00.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.05/2.00 percent versus Tuesday's yield of 2.18/2.13 percent.
One-year was unchanged from Tuesday's yield of 2.30/2.25 percent.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-1/4 3-1/8 percent from 2-3/4 2-5/8 percent.
